questions.text: The working principle of a washing machine is

questions.text: Which of the following is not a vector quantity?
questions.expl: Volume has magnitude only, no direction.

questions.text: A simple machine helps a person in doing
options: The same amount of work with lesser force
The same amount of work slowly
The same amount of work much faster
questions.expl: Simple machines let you do the same work with less applied force.

questions.expl: Displacement has both magnitude and direction.

questions.expl: Momentum has direction, making it a vector quantity.

questions.text: Force is the product of
questions.expl: Newton's second law: Force = mass x acceleration.

questions.text: Energy conservation means
options: Energy could not be created but destroyed
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed
questions.expl: The law of conservation of energy states energy is neither created nor destroyed.

questions.text: In wind power, which form of energy is converted into electrical energy?
questions.expl: Wind's kinetic energy turns turbines to generate electricity.

questions.text: It is difficult to walk on the ice than on the road because
options: Road is harder than the ice
Ice does not offer any reaction when we push with our foot
Ice has a lesser friction than the road
questions.expl: Ice has very low friction, making it hard to walk on.

questions.text: The rain drops are spherical because

questions.text: Oil spreads on water surface because
options: Oil is less dense than water
Surface tension of oil is more than water
Surface tension of oil is less than water
questions.expl: Oil's lower surface tension lets it spread thinly over water.

questions.text: Why is it easier to swim in the sea than in a river?
questions.expl: Salty sea water is denser, giving more buoyancy.

questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is nearly
questions.expl: The speed of light in vacuum is about 3x10^8 m/s.

questions.text: The time taken to reach the Sunlight up to the surface of Earth is approximately
questions.expl: Sunlight takes about 8.5 minutes to reach Earth.

questions.text: For reproducing sound, a CD (Compact Disc) audio player uses a
questions.expl: CD players read data optically using a laser beam.

questions.text: The image formed on Retina is
questions.expl: The eye forms a smaller, inverted image on the retina.

questions.text: The colour of light is determined by its
questions.expl: Wavelength determines the colour of visible light.

questions.text: Which one of the colours has the longest wavelength?
questions.expl: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.text: In the visible spectrum, the colour having the shortest wavelength is
questions.expl: Violet has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.text: The Sun is visible to us a few minutes before the actual sunrise because of
questions.expl: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight, making the sun visible early.

questions.text: Red light is used in traffic signals because
options: It is visible to people even with bad eyesight
questions.expl: Red's long wavelength scatters least, so it's visible from a distance.

questions.text: The Sky appears blue due to
options: The red colour is scattered most
Blue light is minimum absorbed by atmosphere
Red light is ultimately absorbed by atmosphere
questions.expl: Blue light scatters the most in the atmosphere (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.text: The red colour of the Sun at Sunset and Sunrise is due to
questions.expl: Blue light scatters away, leaving red light dominant at sunrise/sunset.

questions.text: Light is made of seven colours. What is the method of separating the colours?
options: The colours can be separated by a prism
The colours can be separated by a filter
The colours can be separated by plants
questions.expl: A prism disperses white light into its seven constituent colours.

questions.text: Which of the following lens is used to minimize Myopia?
questions.expl: Concave (diverging) lenses correct myopia (short-sightedness).

questions.text: In human eye, image of object forms at
questions.expl: The retina is where the image is focused in the human eye.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a part of an atom?
questions.expl: A photon is a particle of light, not a constituent of an atom.

questions.text: A single type of atom is found in
questions.expl: Native elements contain only one type of atom.

questions.text: Constituents of atomic nucleus are
questions.expl: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about molecular structure is correct?
options: Neutron and electron are inside the nucleus and protons revolve around it
Electron and proton are inside the nucleus and neutron revolves around it
Proton and neutron are inside the nucleus and electrons revolve around it
Proton, neutron and electron all are inside the nucleus
questions.expl: Protons and neutrons form the nucleus; electrons orbit around it.

questions.text: The atomic nucleus was discovered by
questions.expl: Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus via his gold foil experiment.

questions.text: In atom, neutron was discovered by
questions.expl: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a subatomic particle?
questions.expl: A deuteron is a nucleus (proton+neutron), not a single subatomic particle.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs constitutes a particle-antiparticle pair?
questions.expl: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron.

questions.text: The alpha particle carries two positive charges. Its mass is very nearly equal to that of
options: Sum of masses of two positrons and two neutrons
Two positrons each carrying a single positive charge
questions.expl: An alpha particle is essentially a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons).

questions.text: The Nucleus of Helium has
questions.expl: A helium nucleus has 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

questions.text: Which of the following carries a negative charge?
questions.expl: Beta particles are fast-moving electrons, carrying negative charge.

questions.text: In an atom, the order of filling up of the orbitals is governed by
questions.expl: Aufbau's principle governs the order of electron filling in orbitals.

questions.text: Regarding the atom of a chemical element, the magnetic quantum number refers to
questions.expl: The magnetic quantum number describes orbital orientation in space.

questions.text: What is the mass number of an element, the atom of which contains two protons, two neutrons and two electrons?
questions.expl: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 2 + 2 = 4.

questions.text: The atoms in which the number of protons is same but the number of neutrons is different, are known as
questions.expl: Isotopes have the same protons but different neutrons.

questions.text: Radioactivity was discovered by
questions.expl: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896.

questions.text: Isotopes are those atoms of the same element which have
options: Atomic mass same but atomic number is different
Atomic mass is different but atomic number is same
Atomic number and atomic mass both are same
questions.expl: Isotopes share atomic number but differ in atomic mass.

questions.text: Radioactivity is measured by
questions.expl: A Geiger counter detects and measures radioactivity.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of chemical change?
options: Dispersion of white light into the light of 7 colours when passed through a prism
Wet soil lamp, when dried, get fragile
questions.expl: Cooking causes a chemical change that softens vegetables.

questions.text: What form of energy is produced in the decomposition of water?
questions.expl: Decomposition of water via electrolysis involves heat and electrical energy.

questions.text: An example of physical change
questions.expl: Dissolving sugar in water is reversible and doesn't change chemical composition.

questions.text: Change of water into vapour is called
questions.expl: Evaporation is a physical change of state.

options: Milk is preserved at a very low temperature for 24 hours
First milk is heated up to a longer time and then cooled suddenly within a specified time

questions.expl: Pasteurization sterilizes milk by controlled heating.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true?
options: Boiling point of any water solution is higher than pure water
Addition of solute to a solution increases its water potential

questions.text: Because of impurities the boiling point of a liquid

options: The atmospheric pressure decreases and hence boiling point is lower
Because of heavy winds in mountains
None of the above is correct
questions.expl: Lower atmospheric pressure at altitude reduces the boiling point.

questions.text: Which type of colloidal system is expressed in the fog?

questions.text: The technique of chromatography is used to
options: Separate the substances from a mixture
